        ### Question
        A 35-year-old woman undergoes a Pap smear after 5 years without prior control and the diagnosis is SIL (high-grade intraepithelial lesion). The correct behavior to follow is:

        ### Options
        opa. Make colposcopy. If it is normal, schedule a conization.
opb. Confirm the cytology with a biopsy of the cervix under colposcopic control.
opc. Repeat cytology to confirm diagnosis.
opd. Make HPV virus typing. Perform conization if the HPV test is positive for high-risk virus.

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: SIL diagnosis -> Perform colposcopy -> Evaluate cervical tissue under magnification -> 95% confidence CHAIN: SIL diagnosis -> Perform colposcopy -> If normal, schedule a conization -> 90% confidence CHAIN: SIL diagnosis -> Confirm with a biopsy of the cervix under colposcopic control -> 95% confidence CHAIN: SIL diagnosis -> Repeat cytology to confirm diagnosis -> 80% confidence CHAIN: SIL diagnosis -> Perform HPV virus typing -> Check for high-risk virus -> Perform conization if positive -> 95%
